## Recall: The Grammar of Graphics

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}

* **data**: dataset that contains the data

* **geom**: geometric shape that the data are mapped to
    + point, line, bar, text, ...
    
* **aes**thetic: visual properties of the **geom** 
    + x position, y position, color, fill, shape
    
* **coord**: coordinate system
    + Cartesian, polar, geographic
    
* **scale**: controls how data are mapped to the visual values of the aesthetic
    + EX: particular colors, linear

* **guide**: legend to help user convert visual display back to the data    

:::

::: {.column width='50%'}

```{r, out.width = "100%", echo=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
include_graphics("img/layers.png") 
```

:::

::::

## ggplot2 example code

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| tidy: false
ggplot(data = ---, mapping = aes(---)) +
  geom_---(---) + 
  coord_---() + 
  scale_---_---() +
  ---
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Example: Over the course of a year, how does the daily number of births vary?

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Load library that has dataset of interest
library(mosaicData)

# Grab data
data(Births2015)

# Load tidyverse (which contains ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)

# Create plot
ggplot(data = Births2015, mapping = aes(x = date, y = births)) + 
  geom_point()
```

::: {.fragment}

* What patterns do you see?

:::

## Example: Cycles related to day of the week? {.smaller}

```{r birthsPlot2}
#| output-location: column
# Create plot
ggplot(data = Births2015, 
       mapping = aes(x = date, y = births, 
                     color = day_of_week)) + 
  geom_point()
```

* Additional aesthetic:
    + Why is this not quite what we want? What do we want?
* What happened to the aspect ratio when we added the legend?
    

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Example: Cycles related to day of the week? {.smaller}

```{r birthsPlot3}
#| output-location: column
# Create plot
ggplot(data = Births2015, 
       mapping = aes(x = date, y = births, 
                     color = wday)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

* Positioning the legend on the bottom of the graph helped give us a nicer aspect ratio.

* What if we want to see the **direction** that the number of births take over time for each day of the week?
    + New visual cue/`geom`?

## Coordinate System Layer

```{r birthsPlot6}
#| output-location: column
library(lubridate)

ggplot(data = Births2015, 
       mapping = aes(x = date, y = births, 
                     color = wday)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_point() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = 
                    as_date(c("2015-01-01",
                              "2015-01-31")))
```

* How did this new layer change our plot?

* What if we want all the points to be colored "midnightblue"?



------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Setting instead of Mapping

```{r birthsPlot7}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = Births2015, 
       mapping = aes(x = date, y = births, 
                     color = "midnightblue")) + 
  geom_point() 
```



------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Setting instead of Mapping

```{r birthsPlot8}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = Births2015, 
       mapping = aes(x = date, y = births)) + 
  geom_point(color = "midnightblue") 
```

* If you want to **set** an aesthetic to a specific value (instead of **mapping** the aesthetic to a variable), do so in the `geom_--()` function.

## Let's explore other **geom**s

* Many are listed on the first page of the [`ggplot2` cheatsheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/cheatsheets/main/data-visualization.pdf).

::: {.fragment .nonincremental}

* Can also ask R:

```{r}
apropos("geom_")
```

:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Adding Curve(s)

```{r birthsPlot12}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = Births2015, 
       mapping = aes(x = date, y = births,
                     color = wday)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

* Does a multiple linear regression line(s) capture the trend?


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Adding Curve(s)

```{r birthsPlot13}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = Births2015, 
       mapping = aes(x = date, y = births,
                     color = wday)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

* The default LOESS smoother usually does a reasonable job.


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Adding Curve(s)

```{r birthsPlot14}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = Births2015, 
       mapping = aes(x = date, y = births,
                     color = wday)) + 
  geom_smooth(color = "black", se = FALSE) +
  geom_point() + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

* What happened?

* Inheriting aesthetics discussion.

## New Example: Movies and the Bechdel Test

* Need a new dataset with more categorical variables

::: {.fragment .nonincremental}

* **The Alison Bechdel Test**: A movie passes the test if:
    + There are at least two named women in the picture
    + They have a conversation with each other at some point
    + That conversation isn't about a male character 

:::

::: {.fragment .nonincremental}

* Movies from 1970 - 2013


```{r}
movies <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2021/2021-03-09/movies.csv') %>%
  filter(rated %in% c("R", "PG-13", "PG", "G"))
```

:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## New Example: Movies and the Bechdel Test

```{r}
glimpse(movies)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = FALSE}

ggplot(data = movies,
       mapping = aes(x = clean_test)) + 
  geom_bar()

ggplot(data = movies, 
       mapping = aes(x = rated, 
                     fill = clean_test)) + 
  geom_bar()

ggplot(data = movies, 
       mapping = aes(x = rated, 
                     fill = clean_test)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill")

ggplot(data = movies, 
       mapping = aes(x = rated, 
                     fill = binary)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill")

movies %>%
  count(rated, binary) %>%
ggplot(mapping = aes(x = rated, binary,
                     fill = n)) + 
  geom_tile()

movies %>%
  group_by(rated, binary) %>%
  summarize(median_budget = mean(budget)) %>%
ggplot(mapping = aes(x = rated, binary,
                     fill = median_budget)) + 
  geom_tile()
```

# What are useful `geom`s for describing amounts/frequencies?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Amounts: `geom_bar`

```{r movies1}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = movies,
       mapping = aes(x = binary)) + 
  geom_bar()
```

* Verbalize the mapping of **data** to **geom_bar()**. 
    + How is this mapping different from **geom_point()**?


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Another option: `geom_col`

```{r movies2}
#| output-location: column
# First wrangle with dplyr
movies_ag <- count(movies, binary) 
movies_ag

ggplot(data = movies_ag, 
       mapping = aes(x = binary, y = n)) + 
  geom_col()
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## `geom_point` again

```{r movies3}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = movies_ag, 
       mapping = aes(x = binary, y = n)) + 
  geom_point(size = 4)
```

* If you are worried about the data-ink ratio...


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## `geom_point` + `geom_segment`

```{r movies4}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = movies_ag, 
       mapping = aes(x = binary, y = n)) + 
  geom_segment(mapping = aes(xend = binary), 
               yend = 0) + 
  geom_point(size = 10, color = "orange") +
  ylim(c(0, 875))
```

* Lollipop chart: compromise?


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Two categorical variables: `geom_bar`

```{r movies5}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = movies,
       mapping = aes(x = rated,
                     fill = binary)) + 
  geom_bar()
```

::: {.nonincremental}

* Describe the mapping.

:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Two categorical variables: `geom_bar`

```{r movies6}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = movies,
       mapping = aes(x = rated,
                     fill = binary)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill")
```

::: {.nonincremental}

* Describe the mapping.

:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Two categorical variables: `geom_bar`

```{r movies6b}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(data = movies,
       mapping = aes(x = rated,
                     fill = binary)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "dodge")
```

::: {.nonincremental}

* Describe the mapping.

:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Two categorical variables: `geom_tile`

```{r movies7}
#| output-location: column
movies_ag <- count(movies, rated, binary)

ggplot(data = movies_ag,
       mapping = aes(x = rated,
                     y = binary,
                     fill = n)) + 
  geom_tile()
```

::: {.nonincremental}

* Describe the mapping.

:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Two categorical variables: `geom_tile`

```{r movies8}
#| output-location: column
movies_ag <- count(movies, rated, binary)

ggplot(data = movies_ag,
       mapping = aes(x = rated,
                     y = binary,
                     fill = n)) + 
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = 4)
```

* Change the `fill` scale!


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Can display more than frequencies!

```{r movies9}
#| output-location: column
movies_ag <- group_by(movies,
                      rated, binary) %>%
  summarize(mean_budget = mean(budget))

ggplot(data = movies_ag,
       mapping = aes(x = rated,
                     y = binary,
                     fill = mean_budget)) + 
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(direction = -1) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Can display more than frequencies!

```{r movies9.2}
#| output-location: column
options(scipen = 999) # turn off scientific notation

movies_ag <- group_by(movies,
                      rated, binary) %>%
  summarize(mean_budget = mean(budget))

ggplot(data = movies_ag,
       mapping = aes(x = rated,
                     y = binary,
                     fill = mean_budget)) + 
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(direction = -1,
                       guide = guide_colorbar(angle = 90)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


# What are useful `geom`s (graphs) for visualizing distributions?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Distributions: `geom_histogram`

```{r movies10}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(movies, aes(x = budget)) +
  geom_histogram()
```

::: {.nonincremental}

* Describe the mapping.

:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Distributions: `geom_histogram`

```{r movies11}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(movies, aes(x = budget)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, 
                 color = "white",
                 fill = "darkcyan") 
```

* Can modify the mapping via the `binwidth` or `bins` arguments


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Distributions: `geom_histogram`

```{r movies12}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(movies, aes(x = budget, 
                   fill = binary)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, 
                 color = "white")
```

* What is problematic about this graph?


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Distributions: `geom_histogram`

```{r movies13}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(movies, aes(x = budget, 
                   fill = binary)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50,
                 alpha = 0.4,
                 position = "identity")
```

::: {.nonincremental}

* Still problematic.

:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## One option: Faceting

```{r movies14}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(movies, aes(x = budget, 
                   fill = binary)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
  facet_wrap(~binary) +
  guides(fill = "none")
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## One option: Faceting

```{r movies14b}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(movies, aes(x = budget, 
                   fill = binary)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  facet_grid(rated ~ binary, scales = "free_y") +
  guides(fill = "none")
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Another option: `geom_density`

```{r movies15}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(movies, aes(x = budget, 
                   fill = binary)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4)  +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Distributions: `geom_boxplot`

```{r movies17}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(movies, aes(x = binary, 
                   y = budget)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Distributions: `geom_boxplot`

```{r movies18}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(movies, aes(x = binary, 
                   y = budget)) +
  geom_boxplot(varwidth = TRUE,
               notch = TRUE)
```

* What does `varwidth` do?
* Why might we add `notch = TRUE`?


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Distributions: `geom_boxplot`

```{r movies19}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(movies, aes(x = binary, 
                   y = budget,
                   fill = rated)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Distributions: `geom_violin`

```{r movies20}
#| output-location: column
ggplot(movies, aes(x = binary, 
                   y = budget)) +
  geom_violin()
```

* Utility of the violin over the box?


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Distributions: `geom_violin`

```{r movies21}
#| output-location: column

ggplot(movies, aes(x = binary, 
                   y = budget)) +
  geom_violin() + 
  geom_jitter(alpha = .1,
              width = .1,
              color = "darkcyan")
```
